tier1.name: node_sources
tier1.detail: 2211 raw references collapse to 2125 distinct — link_sources_tx is INSERT OR IGNORE against the (observation_id, source_id) PK (consolidate.rs:638-650)

tier1.name: entities
tier1.detail: expected folded by this module's own trim+lowercase, not by entities::normalize — a verifier that calls the code it verifies cannot fire. An `entities` row carries no $.legacy key of its own, so it is scoped through the mentions that reach it

tier1.name: documents with the right fact count
tier1.detail: the aggregate node count cannot see a fact filed under the wrong document; this can

tier1.name: import marker
tier1.detail: state = done AND snapshot = this snapshot's hash — a bank imported from a different snapshot is caught rather than counted

tier1.name: consolidation watermark
tier1.detail: one done run per bank whose watermark >= MAX(id) over the MIGRATED nodes — not `= MAX(id)` over the bank, which is true only in the instant between import step 9 and the next row anyone writes. Without such a row the daemon re-consolidates the whole migrated corpus within one poll of restart (consolidate.rs:314-330)

tier1.name: embedding coverage
tier1.detail: a NULL or foreign producer drops a node out of the dense arm silently (search.rs:317, 0005_embedding_model.sql:9-12). Non-zero after --defer-embeddings until the daemon has drained the backlog

tier1.name: semantic edges from observations
tier1.detail: parity, not a divergence: legacy stores none either — /graph decomposed by endpoint fact_type gives 4,603 == /stats 4,603 for bank-a

tier1.name: temporal self-consistency
tier1.detail: 105199 stored against 105199 the rule produces: 0 stored edges it would not emit, 0 it emits that are not stored, over 5 of 5 banks. links.rs:62-92 replayed over the migrated nodes' own (fact_type, event_date) — this replaces the equality against legacy that can never hold

tier2.name: temporal, fact to fact
tier2.note: legacy's /stats temporal count is fact-to-fact: it stores no derived edge on an observation (relink filters fact_type IN ('experience','world'), pg/graph.py:606). Its neighbour query applies no 24h predicate where links.rs:69 does, so the sets differ by rule and not by ordering

tier2.name: temporal, observation to observation
tier2.note: a new edge class: legacy has no counterpart, so there is no ratio to take. Folding these into the fact-to-fact ratio would pass a run in which the fact-edge rule silently broke

tier2.name: semantic
tier2.note: NO BAND, deliberately. Every semantic edge here connects two nodes embedded in the same batch of 8: embed_task.rs:178-179 builds node_types from the just-embedded batch and links.rs:143 drops every neighbour outside it. Over the same vectors a whole-corpus pass emits ~10x more. Banding this would be banding a CE-7 defect

tier2.name: proof_count disagreements
tier2.note: reported, never gated: legacy's stored value falls back to len(source_ids) (export.py:457) and ours is derived from what survived the INSERT OR IGNORE. They are different schemas, not a resolution bug

entity links.citation: engine/memories/pg/counts.py:47-49 — derived at /stats time, not stored; links.rs:6-8 is our matching decision

sentence: No fact, observation, document or authored causal relation was lost. Derived adjacency (semantic, temporal) was rebuilt from the migrated facts by MemGarden's own rules rather than copied: a semantic edge is a function of the vector space and ours is not legacy's, and legacy's temporal rule applies no 24-hour window to its neighbour query (ops_postgresql.py:562-593) where ours does. The rebuilt temporal set reproduces our own rule exactly (105199 edges, checked against a reference implementation) and its fact-to-fact half stands at 1.61x legacy's count; semantic stands at 0.11x, and that ratio is a CE-7 defect rather than a migration property — every semantic edge here is confined to one embedding batch. Observation-to-observation temporal edges (34876) are a class legacy does not store. Entity links exist in neither system's storage.
